$comment: T-RESUME-SW-KEY-RACE vectors (RESUME-PROTOCOL v3.0 RULE 30).
THE ROW THIS FILE EXISTS FOR is prod-swbridge-none-pair-resumed. On PROD 9ca5ba7
(live-acceptance 20:10Z) the lab pair was formed BEFORE the service worker had
registered its key - the page logged `advert recipients=1 swBridge=none` at
20:13:50Z, so the transcript carried NO extension recipient. The browser was then
restarted on the same profile inside the relay's 180 s soft hold; the relay
auto-resumed the pair (gap=4979 ms), the page published PAIRING_ACTIVE resumed:true
at 20:15:16.706Z, and 220 ms later the M-A5-3 coverage guard left the room:
[E2E] re-pair-needed - the SAS transcript carries an extension key the service
worker no longer reports (M-A5-3)
-> leaveActive -> relay terminateActivePair: user_left -> the phone's E2E torn down,
with the copy 'This browser's keys were cleared' - which was false. Nothing was
cleared. The restarted SW had simply come up WITH a key that the older transcript
never carried, and the old predicate read that as a stale advert.
Two consumers were intended (RULE 30). Only one exists:
- WEB/SW: tests/e2e-resume-sw-key-race.test.mjs drives the REAL sasCoverage,
swKeyGuardVerdict and awaitSwKeyAnswer from hooks/phoneE2e.ts - the same three
functions hooks/useE2e.ts onPairingActive calls, in the same order - on a
VIRTUAL clock, plus the REAL user-facing copy from lib/encryptedModeCopy.ts.
- PHONE: THERE IS NO KOTLIN TWIN, and this is a statement rather than an omission.
The M-A5-3 coverage guard is a page-side rule about what the DISPLAYED digits
cover; the Android side has no mirror of it (`grep -rn 'coversSw|staleSwKey|A5-3'
dnkdialer-android/app/src` is empty at 9ca5ba7). The phone's role in this defect
is passive - it receives PAIRING_TERMINATED from a relay that was told user_left.
A Kotlin file asserting these rows would be a second implementation of a rule the
phone does not have, which is the duplicated-predicate mistake A3 exists about.
FIELDS
transcript   recipKeys, symbolically: phone | web | ext-live | ext-other.
`ext-live` is the key the SW reports; `ext-other` is a different
extension key (a swapped/stale advert).
resumed      the relay's PAIRING_ACTIVE `resumed` bit.
swAnswer     what the bridge eventually answers: present-live | present-other |
absent | never (the grace runs out in silence).
answerAtMs   when it lands, on the virtual clock, relative to the guard starting.
expect.leave/error   the verdict. `null` error means the pair is KEPT.
expect.coversSw      what the badge says about the extension leg either way.
expect.waitedMs      how long the grace actually cost. A row that answers at 0 ms
must cost NOTHING - a fix that made every resume sleep 5 s would pass
a leave/stay-only assertion and be unusable.
THE BUG ROWS ARE KEPT DELIBERATELY. prod-swbridge-none-pair-resumed and
resumed-ext-key-arrives-late are the two that were red on 9ca5ba7; delete either and
the suite still prints a cheerful N/N while a resumed room is torn down again on
live acceptance. The floor in tools/e2e-gate.mjs is what makes that deletion fail.

rows.name: resumed-ext-key-arrives-at-0ms
rows.why: The SW had already answered before the guard ran. No re-query, no grace, no leave.

rows.name: resumed-ext-key-arrives-at-1s
rows.why: A cold-started MV3 worker answering inside the grace. The pair STAYS, and the wait ends when the answer lands - not at the cap.

rows.name: resumed-ext-key-arrives-late
rows.why: The grace ran out with the bridge silent. THAT is a verdict, and its reason is the restart - never 'your keys were cleared'.

rows.name: prod-swbridge-none-pair-resumed
rows.why: PROD 9ca5ba7. The transcript carries NO extension recipient (recipients=1, swBridge=none), and the restarted SW comes up WITH a key. Nothing was advertised, so nothing is stale: the pair is KEPT and the badge honestly says the digits do not cover the extension.

rows.name: resumed-no-ext-recipient-sw-silent
rows.why: Same 2-key transcript, and the SW never answers at all. Still nothing to be stale about, and no grace is spent on a question that cannot change the answer.

rows.name: resumed-sw-reports-a-different-key
rows.why: M-A5-3 AS WRITTEN, unchanged: an advertised extension key the SW cannot back. A swapped key is what 're-pair-needed' copy is actually about, so this row keeps it.

rows.name: resumed-sw-definitively-has-no-key
rows.why: The SW answered, and the answer was 'I hold no key', against a transcript that advertised one. Refusal - and the reason is the extension's state, not a cleared browser.

rows.name: fresh-pair-stale-advert-still-refuses
rows.why: CONTROL. The fix is about WHEN the guard decides, not WHAT it means: on a first connect a stale advert refuses exactly as it did before this lane.

rows.name: fresh-pair-no-ext-recipient
rows.why: CONTROL. The swBridge=none first connect that INC-0923 produces every time. It paired fine before this lane and must still pair fine.

rows.name: fresh-pair-sw-silent-with-ext-recipient
rows.why: CONTROL. `unknown` on a NON-resumed pair is still not a verdict: no grace is served and the pair is kept, which is the pre-existing behaviour this lane must not widen.
